decisions.reason: Coverage finding adopted as the basis for retaining the daily cross-sectional setup: rows_by_symbol shows 59 rows per symbol, common_dates=59 equals union_dates=59, missing_from_observed_union is empty for every symbol, and the observed window runs 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-30, so the raw 5-observation trailing return is defined identically per name on every observed date with no filling. The observed union is not an exchange calendar and no filling or corporate-action inference is permitted, which supports leaving the spec untouched rather than altering eligibility or windows.

Normalization finding adopted: raw 5-observation scores are dimensionless simple returns on the same unadjusted-close scale and are arithmetically comparable across the three names, and no frozen source shows them incomparable. The observed dispersion heterogeneity (sample_sd_score 0.031358036156655944 / 0.02601465514066781 / 0.025036106969249714) is the only motivation for realized-volatility normalization and remains an unproven hypothesis; per source_contract, normalization "does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk", and the sources provide no formal evaluation or proof that a revision is better. normalization="none" and volatility_window=null are therefore retained; normalization="realized_volatility" with any volatility_window is explicitly rejected as unsupported.

Timing finding adopted: lookback=5 is arithmetically coherent with the frozen sample — 59 observations per symbol and a 6-trailing-observation requirement leave exactly 54 eligible signals per symbol (insufficient_past_observations=5), of which 53 have a next observed close because the 2026-10-30 final row has no later observation. Any longer lookback (schema maximum 20) would only shrink the 54-signal eligible sample and no frozen source evidences a preferable length. lookback=5 is retained; any other lookback value is explicitly rejected as unsupported.

Interpretation finding adopted: direction=+1 remains an unproven momentum hypothesis — mixed descriptive mean scores are description, not sign evidence; the sources contain no volume, corporate-action, calendar or forward-return-label data on a small convenience sample with no alpha or superiority proof; and close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions (largest absolute one-observation returns 0.05555555555555547, 0.03643842353519777, 0.03267973856209161), so no evidence-based max absolute daily return cap exists. direction=1 and max_absolute_daily_return=null are retained; direction=-1 and any non-null cap are explicitly rejected as unsupported hypotheses, since no substantive spec change is justified by this descriptive evidence.

body.rationale: Decision: RETAIN the initial candidate unchanged; no source-supported finding justifies a substantive change. Exact retained spec fields: lookback=5, direction=1, normalization="none", volatility_window=null, max_absolute_daily_return=null. Evidence basis, disposing of all four findings: (1) Finding a25302fbed1933cb5eab4ab1c8ed1bf360bd13e1c53e78e429d7acf5593dd9d7 (coverage, adopt): the panel supports a daily cross-sectional comparison on every one of the 59 observed dates (rows_by_symbol 59 per name; common_dates=59 equals union_dates=59; missing_from_observed_union empty for all three symbols; window 2026-08-03 to 2026-10-30), so the daily cross-sectional use of this spec is arithmetically defined with no filling; the observed union is not an exchange calendar and no filling or corporate-action inference is permitted. (2) Finding cf4d7ae100beddd7222607d95ee44e33eefbeb3a7c0fd9b7e6da5a9d2d66353f (normalization, adopt): raw 5-observation scores are dimensionless simple returns on the same unadjusted-close scale and are arithmetically comparable across the three names; the observed dispersion heterogeneity (sample_sd_score 0.031358036156655944 for 000651.XSHE, 0.02601465514066781 for 600000.XSHG, 0.025036106969249714 for 600519.XSHG, versus sample_sd_one_observation_return 0.01369940691247741, 0.012486459027152721 and 0.01289591113463477) motivates realized-volatility normalization only as an unproven hypothesis, because normalization "does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk" and the descriptive sources neither prove it is required nor prove it improves comparability; normalization=none is therefore retained. (3) Finding 38a05aa03ce2f2cfe3e17363b879aeec8c195980d0bc2ac368b5fafc6579405c (timing, adopt): lookback=5 is arithmetically coherent — 59 observations per symbol minus 6 required trailing observations leaves exactly 54 eligible signals per symbol, of which 53 have a next observed close because the 2026-10-30 last row has no later observation; windows use past observed rows with no filling; any longer lookback (schema maximum 20) would only shrink the 54-signal eligible sample with no frozen source evidencing a preferable length, so lookback=5 is retained. (4) Finding 0b525b04b74181383ffc909ebf0abf1602be39f92fa20a4e044c1fff119fe20d (interpretation, adopt): direction=+1 remains an unproven momentum hypothesis — mixed descriptive mean scores are description, not sign evidence; the sources contain no volume, corporate actions, delisted universe, point-in-time membership, bid/ask, transaction costs, official calendar or forward return labels; and close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions (largest absolute one-observation returns: 000651.XSHE 41.58 to 39.27 = 0.05555555555555547; 600519.XSHG 1341.99 to 1293.09 = 0.03643842353519777; 600000.XSHG 9.18 to 9.48 = 0.03267973856209161), so no evidence-based max_absolute_daily_return cap exists and direction=+1 is retained unchanged. Explicit rejection of unsupported alternatives: any lookback other than 5, direction=-1, normalization="realized_volatility" (with any non-null volatility_window), and any non-null max_absolute_daily_return are all rejected as unsupported hypotheses on the current sources; a change in score scale would not establish alpha, superiority, removal of systematic risk or corporate-action handling, and no revision is proven better.
